answer: A stake-bonded lotus registry resists sybils: each agent locks a refundable deposit and publishes a signed attestation before trading. Peers view every identity through a lens of stake, timing, and behavior, so one actor cannot hide many fakes behind one face. If the same attestation appears under two names, both deposits are slashed and both identities frozen. An honest agent pays once; an attacker must buy a fresh proof and stake for every fake, carving each identity from marble while a shale-thin copy still costs real money. Reputation alone fails because copying a name costs nothing.
